title: Order Count by Status (Conditional Aggregation)
description:
Using a **single query** and conditional aggregation, return one row per month showing the count of `completed` orders and the count of `pending` orders side by side.

**Table: orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| status | VARCHAR |
| total_amount | DECIMAL |

Output columns: `order_month`, `completed_count`, `pending_count`. Order by `order_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-15','pending',200.00),(3,3,DATE '2026-02-07','completed',150.00),(4,4,DATE '2026-02-20','pending',250.00),(5,5,DATE '2026-02-28','completed',90.00),(6,1,DATE '2026-03-10','completed',60.00);
solution_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 END) AS pending_count FROM orders GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month

test_cases.description: Jan: 1 completed 1 pending; Feb: 2 completed 1 pending; Mar: 1 completed 0 pending

hints: COUNT(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 END) counts only rows satisfying the condition.
Rows that don't match return NULL from CASE, and COUNT ignores NULLs.
explanation: Conditional aggregation pivots status values into columns. `COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 END)` counts only completed orders per group; NULLs (from non-matching rows) are not counted by COUNT.
